findings.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse wrapper object ({success, data}), and this call site stores that wrapper directly as the credential key (`data: { key }`), whereas the replaced code `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` stored the parsed data itself. On the first Google token refresh of any deployment (sync mode or not), credential.key is overwritten with {success:true,data:{...}}; every later read of credential.key.access_token/expiry_date returns undefined, so Google Calendar API calls fail authorization and the calendar stays broken until the user manually reconnects the app.

[BUG] In sync mode the helper returns the raw fetch Response object, but the call sites it was grafted onto consume the response shapes of their original refresh mechanisms (axios `.data` for zoho-bigin/zohocrm, google-auth-library `.res.data` for google, the Hubspot SDK token object), so the sync path is structurally incompatible with those callers. With CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set (exactly the setup .env.example documents), google/zoho-bigin/zohocrm throw TypeErrors on every token refresh and hubspot persists undefined token fields; the credential-sync feature cannot work for these apps as shipped.

[BUG] In sync mode `res` is a fetch Response, which has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` on the next line throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'access_token'). Every google-calendar token refresh crashes when credential sync is enabled; the surrounding catch turns it into a failed calendar operation, so google calendars never obtain a working access token under sync.

[BUG] In sync mode `tokenInfo` is a fetch Response whose `.data` is undefined, so `tokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). zoho-bigin token refresh crashes on every attempt when credential sync is enabled, leaving the integration with expired tokens and no way to renew them.

[BUG] In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a fetch Response whose `.data` is undefined, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). zohocrm token refresh crashes on every attempt when credential sync is enabled, breaking Zoho CRM calendar sync entirely for sync-enabled deployments.

[BUG] In sync mode the value awaited into `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` is a raw fetch Response, and a fetch Response has none of the HubspotToken fields (access token / refresh token) that the subsequent code reads and persists into credential.key. Each sync-mode hubspot refresh writes a credential key whose token fields are undefined, permanently breaking the hubspot integration for affected users until manual reconnection.

[BUG] The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (the second silently overwrites the first), so this is a plain object schema with a literal "[object Object]" key — not the intended index signature — and safeParse strips every property except access_token. Sync-mode refreshes persist credentials with no expiry data despite the comment claiming number properties are kept: office365calendar re-stores its stale pre-refresh expiry_date so expiry-gated refresh logic re-fires on every use (a sync-endpoint round trip per calendar operation), salesforce's stored key loses instance_url, and zoom loses expires_in.

[BUG] The call passes `credentialId` — an identifier no other call site uses (all seven sibling sites pass `credential.userId`, matching the helper's `userId` parameter) and which is not defined in the visible scope — so tsc fails with "Cannot find name 'credentialId'". packages/app-store fails to compile and the PR cannot build as-is; if a like-named binding exists outside the hunk, the sync endpoint receives the credential row id instead of the cal.com user id and resolves the wrong user's credentials.

[BUG] In sync mode `resp` is the sync endpoint's response whose documented body is `{access_token, expiry_date}`, not lark's `{code, msg, data}` envelope that `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` validates. handleLarkError sees code !== 0 (undefined) and throws, so lark-calendar token refresh fails on every attempt when credential sync is enabled.

[BUG] The sync endpoint's response body (access token plus expiry date per the documented contract) does not contain the ITokenResponse fields (`expires_in`, `refresh_token`) this adapter reads after handleErrorsJson. expiry_date computed from undefined becomes NaN (or stays stale), so the adapter stops refreshing and MS Teams meeting creation fails with expired tokens once the current access token lapses.

[BUG] In sync mode the body returned by handleWebexResponse is the sync endpoint's `{access_token, expiry_date}` payload, which lacks the webex token-response fields (refresh_token, expires_in) the adapter reads to rebuild the credential key. Webex credentials are re-stored without valid expiry/refresh data, so webex meeting creation degrades to failures once the initial access token expires.

[ADVISORY] Success is decided by `response.statusText !== "OK"`; undici's fetch returns an empty statusText when the response carries no reason phrase (e.g. over HTTP/2 or via certain proxies), so a valid 200 response is treated as a failure. Salesforce token refresh intermittently throws HttpError 400 on successful responses depending on protocol/proxy path; `response.ok` (or a status check) is the reliable predicate.

[ADVISORY] The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is dead code — parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on parse failure, so success is always true at this point. Maintainers are misled into thinking there is a non-throwing path; the Promise.reject line can never execute and will rot on the next refactor.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds three non-trivial dual-mode modules (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, and the /api/webhook/app-credential handler) and no test in the diff exercises either branch of any of them. The sync-mode contract mismatches reported above (fetch Response vs axios/SDK shapes, schema field stripping) are exactly what one unit test per helper would have caught; future edits to the env-flag branching will silently break one mode again.

[ADVISORY] The removed `console.error` block logged the zod error and the raw Microsoft response on schema failure; the replacement throws a generic Error('Invalid refreshed tokens were returned') with no diagnostic detail, and it now aborts the refresh where the old code logged and continued. Operators debugging Outlook token failures lose the response body that explained the mismatch, and transient schema mismatches now fail the calendar operation instead of proceeding with the previous token.

[BUG] When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint, and this code reads `res?.data` (undefined on a Response, the body is never .json()-parsed) then dereferences `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError on every refresh. Every Google Calendar token refresh in a credential-sharing deployment throws TypeError, so calendar sync fails for all users as soon as access tokens expire (~hourly).

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}), not the parsed payload, and this code stores that wrapper object directly as credential.key, changing the stored key shape from {access_token, expiry_date, ...} to {success: true, data: {...}}. After the first token refresh (in both sync and non-sync modes), every subsequent read of credential.key.access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date returns undefined, permanently breaking Google Calendar for that user until the DB row is manually repaired.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the result is typed and consumed as HubspotToken (the unchanged downstream reads .expires_in/.access_token/.refresh_token and never calls .json()), yielding undefined token fields and a NaN expiry. With credential sharing enabled, every HubSpot token refresh persists access_token: undefined and expiryDate: NaN (or throws serializing NaN), breaking HubSpot calendar sync for all synced users.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this axios-based code reads `tokenInfo.data.error`; fetch Responses have no `.data` property, so the line throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes on every invocation in credential-sharing deployments, breaking Bigin calendar sync entirely.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this axios-based code reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`; fetch Responses have no `.data` property, so the line throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho CRM token refresh crashes on every invocation in credential-sharing deployments, breaking Zoho CRM calendar sync entirely.

[BUG] The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (zod schemas do not implement toString for key generation), so the schema collapses to {access_token, "[object Object]"} and, because z.object strips unknown keys, the expiry field the comment says to capture is never kept. In sync mode every refreshed credential is persisted without its expiry (office365-calendar and zoom then see a stale/past expiry on every call and re-hit the sync endpoint each time), and a sync response containing no expiry at all passes validation despite the documented contract.

[BUG] Schema selection is keyed only on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but the response passed in only originates from the sync endpoint when userId is truthy (refreshOAuthTokens' extra gate) or when the app uses refreshOAuthTokens at all (salesforce never does), so direct-OAuth responses get parsed with the minimum sync schema. Team-scoped credentials (userId null) for office365-calendar/zoom get their real refresh_token overwritten with the 'refresh_token' placeholder and their expiry stripped on first refresh, so the next direct refresh authenticates with a fake token and the credential is bricked; in sync mode salesforce's stored key loses instance_url/issued_at/signature, breaking subsequent jsforce connections.

[BUG] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body), symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse all throw on malformed or wrongly-encrypted payloads with no try/catch, so a request with a valid secret but an invalid or undecryptable body returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. Any malformed webhook delivery or parent/child encryption-key mismatch produces unhandled 500s (with stack traces in dev) instead of a descriptive 400, and retrying senders hammer the endpoint with non-actionable failures.

[BUG] No test-shaped file exists anywhere in this diff (no spec/**, test/**, *.test.* or *.spec.* files), yet the diff adds three pieces of behavior-bearing logic with zero coverage: the webhook endpoint's secret-check/validation/upsert flow, parseRefreshTokenResponse's dual-schema selection, and refreshOAuthTokens' sync-vs-direct routing. None of the sync-mode behavior (which the findings above show is broken at 4 of 9 call sites and corrupts credentials at 2 more) can be caught by CI; any regression in the secret check or credential upsert ships silently to self-hosters.

[BUG] This call site passes `credentialId` as the sync request's calcomUserId while all eight other call sites pass credential.userId; credentialId in this scope is the credential row id, so sync-mode requests carry the wrong identifier. In credential-sharing deployments the sync endpoint receives the credential's DB id instead of the user id and returns tokens for the wrong user (or fails), breaking Zoho Bigin sync and potentially cross-wiring tokens between users.

[ADVISORY] The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication material (no secret header, no signature) — only calcomUserId and appSlug — so the protocol as implemented gives the endpoint no way to authenticate the caller. Unless the self-hoster invents out-of-band protection (nothing in this diff or .env.example provides it), a reachable sync endpoint dispenses live OAuth access tokens for any userId, making userId enumeration a token-harvesting vector.

[ADVISORY] A Salesforce token refresh is now executed unconditionally on every service instantiation — not routed through refreshOAuthTokens like the other eight apps — and success is detected via `response.statusText !== "OK"`, which is empty under HTTP/2 or reason-phrase-stripping proxies. Every calendar operation pays an extra Salesforce round-trip even when the stored token is valid; behind an HTTP/2 proxy the check throws 400 on successful responses; and in sync mode the refresh bypasses the sync endpoint, diverging from the protocol the rest of this PR implements.

[ADVISORY] lark, msteams (office365video) and webex route refreshes through refreshOAuthTokens but never apply parseRefreshTokenResponse, so the sync endpoint's response is consumed through legacy error handlers with no schema validation and no refresh_token placeholder injection. A sync response missing app-specific fields (e.g. lark's refresh_token/expire, webex's expires_in) is persisted verbatim into credential.key, silently degrading those integrations in sync mode.

[ADVISORY] The webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual), exposing a timing side channel on the secret check. An attacker making many requests against the credential-sync endpoint can in principle recover the webhook secret byte-by-byte, gaining the ability to write arbitrary credential keys into any user's account.

[ADVISORY] The findFirst-then-update-else-create sequence is not atomic and no uniqueness constraint is enforced on (userId, appId) here, so concurrent or retried webhook deliveries for the same user+app can create duplicate credentials. Duplicate credential rows for the same user+app make later findFirst results nondeterministic, so bookings can run against a stale token while the fresh one sits unused.

[ADVISORY] The configured header name is used as-is to index req.headers, but Node lowercases all incoming header names, so an env value like 'Calcom-Webhook-Secret' looks up a key that never exists. A self-hoster setting the header name in conventional casing gets a 403 'Invalid webhook secret' on every request despite a correct secret, with the only hint being a comment in .env.example.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response object, but callers written against provider SDKs expect already-parsed payloads (google-auth-library `res.data`, axios `tokenInfo.data`, hubspot `HubspotToken`), so enabling credential sharing breaks token refresh for those integrations. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, Google Calendar throws a TypeError at `token.access_token` (res.data is undefined), Zoho Bigin and ZohoCRM throw at `tokenInfo.data.error`, and Hubspot spreads the raw Response into the stored credential key (yielding no token fields); lark/office365/webex/zoom parse the sync endpoint's minimal JSON against provider-shaped handlers and lose expiry/refresh fields — the PR's core feature breaks refresh for the apps it claims to enhance.

[BUG] With credential sharing enabled, `res` is the sync endpoint's fetch Response, so `res?.data` evaluates to undefined and `token.access_token` on the next line throws a TypeError, making every Google Calendar token refresh fail. Any deployment with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED enabled gets a thrown TypeError instead of a refreshed Google token, so Google Calendar availability and booking flows fail once tokens expire.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{success, data}`), and this call site stores that wrapper directly as the credential `key` (the replaced code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`'s data), corrupting the credential shape on every refresh. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}`; the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation reads `credential.key.access_token` as undefined and Google Calendar auth fails — for all deployments, independent of whether the sync feature is enabled.

[BUG] Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential row identifier) as the userId/calcomUserId argument, while every other call site in this diff passes `credential.userId`, so Bigin sync requests carry the wrong identifier. The parent application keys its credential store on calcomUserId; receiving a credential row id means Bigin sync lookups fail, or if a row id numerically matches another user's id, the parent returns a different user's OAuth credentials to this user's session.

[BUG] Both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the same '[object Object]' string, so the second declaration overwrites the first and the schema validates nothing beyond `access_token`; with zod's default unknown-key stripping, sync-mode `.data` contains only `access_token`. The commented intent ('any property with a number is the expiry') is not implemented: Salesforce's refreshed credential is persisted without `instance_url` (its next jsforce.Connection cannot reach the API), and Office365's spread `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` now contributes only access_token, so the stored expiry is never advanced and every subsequent call re-triggers a sync-endpoint refresh.

[BUG] The hand-rolled Salesforce token refresh is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely, unlike every other integration in this diff. With the feature off, every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation now performs an eager token-endpoint round-trip plus a credential-table write on the path jsforce previously refreshed lazily (extra remote call + DB write on every availability/booking operation); with the feature on, Salesforce never consults CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, so it is the one OAuth app the sync feature silently does not cover.

[BUG] In sync mode `tokenInfo` is a fetch Response rather than an axios response, so `tokenInfo.data` is undefined and `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` throws a TypeError reading 'error' of undefined. Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes whenever credential sharing is enabled, failing Bigin calendar sync at the first expired token.

[BUG] In sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a fetch Response rather than an axios response, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError reading 'error' of undefined. Zoho CRM token refresh crashes whenever credential sharing is enabled, failing Zoho CRM calendar sync at the first expired token.

[ADVISORY] The outbound sync request sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret or auth header, while the push direction (the app-credential webhook) is guarded by CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET — the pull half of the protocol enforces no authentication. Self-hosters following the .env.example documentation must expose CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT returning raw OAuth access tokens; with no auth modeled by the shipped client, the natural implementation returns any user's fresh credentials to any caller who can reach the endpoint and enumerate userIds.

[ADVISORY] The webhook persists the decrypted `keys` JSON verbatim as the credential key without validating it against the target app's credential schema (e.g. googleCredentialSchema). A parent app pushing a stale, partially-migrated, or malformed payload silently corrupts the user's stored credentials; the failure surfaces later as runtime errors inside calendar/video services, far from the write that caused it.

[ADVISORY] None of the new sync logic in this diff — the webhook handler's auth/decrypt/upsert, refreshOAuthTokens' mode branching, or parseRefreshTokenResponse's dual-schema parse — is covered by any test added here. The sync-mode TypeErrors in google/zoho-bigin/zohocrm and the wrapper-storage corruption are each unit-testable in isolation and would have been caught before shipping a feature whose enablement breaks bookings.

[BUG] `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throw on malformed or undecryptable input with no try/catch, so the endpoint returns a generic 500 instead of a 4xx. A parent app sending a bad payload (wrong encryption key, non-JSON keys) gets an opaque 500 with no diagnostic, and each attempt logs a stack trace server-side instead of rejecting with the 400 the request contract implies.

[ADVISORY] The redirectUri change from `${appConfig.slug}` to the hardcoded 'zoho-bigin' is behavior-preserving cleanup unrelated to the credential-sync feature. Unrelated churn inside a 30-file PR: reviewers must trace why an OAuth redirect line changed in a credential-sync change, and the config.json slug stops being the single source of truth for the callback URL.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseResult wrapper ({success, data}), but this call site stores that wrapper as the entire credential key, whereas the replaced googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) returned the parsed credentials object directly. After the first token refresh (in both sync and non-sync modes), credential.key becomes {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the credentials object; every reader of credential.key.access_token / .expiry_date gets undefined, so Google Calendar operations fail for the affected user until the row is manually repaired.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh under credential sharing crashes instead of refreshing, so synced google-calendar credentials fail all calendar operations once their initial expiry passes.

[BUG] The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to fixed literal strings (Object.prototype.toString, i.e. '[object Object]'), not a catchall, so minimumTokenResponseSchema is a fixed-shape object that keeps only access_token and strips every other field — the expiry the adjacent comments promise is never captured. In sync mode every refreshed token is persisted without a fresh expiry (spread-based call sites like office365 and zoom retain the stale old expiryDate), so expiry-gated refresh fires on every calendar operation, hammering CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with one external call plus a credential write per request, or the expiry is undefined and 401s surface instead.

[BUG] When the parsed token has no refresh_token, the helper fabricates the literal string 'refresh_token' and the persisting call sites (google, office365calendar, zoomvideo spread it into the stored key) write it over the credential's real refresh token. In sync mode the stored refresh_token is destroyed on first refresh; any later fallback to local refresh — team credentials (userId null, which refreshOAuthTokens explicitly routes to the real refreshFunction) or an operator disabling credential sharing — authenticates with the literal 'refresh_token', the provider rejects it, and the credential is permanently broken until re-authentication.

[BUG] In sync mode the helper returns the raw fetch Response while each caller's fallback path returns a different type (google: GaxiosResponse .res, hubspot: HubspotToken, zoho: axios response), so no call site can consume both modes with one shape and the one-size sync contract cannot represent the per-provider token domains (expires_in vs expiry_date, refresh_token, instance_url). Every call site that does not natively consume a fetch Response breaks in sync mode — google crashes on token.access_token, hubspot wipes the credential key, zoho-bigin/zohocrm throw on .data.error, and the lark/msteams/webex parsers receive a body shape (access_token + expiry only) that lacks the provider fields they read.

[BUG] In sync mode the fetch Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens is bound to HubspotToken, so expiresIn/accessToken reads yield undefined and the persisted key collapses to {expiryDate: NaN} because a fetch Response has no own enumerable properties to spread. The first Hubspot token refresh under credential sharing wipes the stored credential key, destroying the access and refresh tokens and breaking the integration until the user re-authenticates.

[BUG] The third argument passed to refreshOAuthTokens is credentialId (the credential row id) where the parameter is userId and every other call site in the diff passes credential.userId. The sync request carries calcomUserId=<credential id>, so the parent endpoint resolves the wrong (or no) user and can return another user's tokens into this credential row; team credentials also take the sync path because credentialId is always truthy, where every other app falls back to local refresh for them.

[BUG] In sync mode tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and the unchanged downstream check !tokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError. Zoho Bigin token refresh under credential sharing always fails, so synced credentials cannot refresh and calendar operations fail once the initial token expires.

[BUG] In sync mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and the unchanged check !zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError. Zoho CRM token refresh under credential sharing always fails, so synced credentials cannot refresh and calendar operations fail once the initial token expires.

[BUG] In sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips instance_url (and every field except access_token) from the Salesforce refresh response, and this update persists that stripped object as the credential key. After one refresh the stored key no longer contains instance_url, so the next connection creation reads credentialKey.instance_url as undefined and the jsforce connection cannot reach the Salesforce instance — Salesforce breaks from the second use onward under credential sharing.

[BUG] A token refresh (external POST to login.salesforce.com plus a credential UPDATE) now runs unconditionally on every connection creation, where previously the jsforce.Connection was constructed locally and refreshed lazily by jsforce on 401. Every availability check or booking flow that instantiates the service now pays a Salesforce token-endpoint round trip and a DB write even when the token is valid, and concurrent service instances race duplicate refreshes and writes on the same credential row.

[BUG] The handler trusts the parent's raw numeric userId to identify the local user (the schema comment says 'UserId of the cal.com user') with no cross-instance identity mapping or verification such as an email check. Unless the child instance's user id space is kept identical to cal.com's, the webhook delivers one cal.com user's OAuth credentials to the local user holding the same numeric id — a different person — who then books meetings through another user's calendar; any user created or deleted on either side diverges the id spaces and nothing in the design detects it.

[BUG] The findFirst-then-create sequence is a check-then-insert race with no UNIQUE(userId, appId) constraint backing it (the in-code claim that upsert is impossible is exactly the missing unique key), and the (userId, appId) slot also has a second writer in the local OAuth callback. Two concurrent webhook deliveries (e.g., a reconnect racing an in-flight sync) both miss the findFirst and create duplicate Credential rows for the same user and app, and the findFirst can also overwrite the key of a locally-installed credential; consumers binding to a stale duplicate use dead tokens.

[BUG] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws ZodError unhandled, and there is no method guard so req.body is undefined on GET, returning a 500 for malformed requests while the handler's own 403/404 paths establish a 4xx contract. Any malformed POST — or any GET — to /api/webhook/app-credential returns a 500 instead of a 400, masking client errors as server faults.

[ADVISORY] The credential-sync endpoint becomes a hard, unguarded dependency of the token-refresh path: the fetch has no timeout, no response.ok check, and the design provides no fallback once the placeholder refresh token has replaced the real one. If the parent cal.com instance is slow or down, every calendar operation needing a refresh hangs (Node fetch has no default timeout) or fails with an HTML error page flowing into the token parsers — a cascading failure across all shared-credential apps with no degradation path.

[ADVISORY] The child-to-parent sync request carries no authentication material — no secret header or signature, only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body — so the integration contract as defined can only be served by an endpoint that authenticates callers out of band or not at all. Self-hosters following the .env.example stand up a credential-delivery endpoint whose contract gives it nothing to authenticate the caller with; access control is left entirely to deployment-specific mechanisms the shipped client never exercises.

[ADVISORY] Salesforce is the only refreshed app not routed through refreshOAuthTokens — it refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com even when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured. A parallel refresh path contradicts the feature's own architecture: self-hosters configuring sync still get direct Salesforce calls from the child using parent-shared refresh tokens, and credential rotation performed on the parent never propagates to salesforce credentials.

[ADVISORY] The new sync-mode branching logic (mode-dependent schema selection, placeholder injection, wrapper return shape) ships with no test anywhere in the diff, and the google call site already mis-binds its return value. Regressions in this helper corrupt persisted credentials across every calendar and video app at once; a single test asserting the returned shape and the persisted key would have caught the google wrapper bug before ship.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted keys payload is persisted without validating it against the target app's credential schema (each app ships one, e.g. googleCredentialSchema), and a decryption or JSON.parse failure surfaces as an unhandled 500. Parent/child version skew or a buggy parent silently persists malformed credentials that only fail at booking time, far from the write that caused them; a schema parse at this boundary would reject bad payloads with a 400.

[ADVISORY] The !accessTokenParsed.success branch is dead code — parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on parse failure, so the Promise.reject is unreachable. The unreachable branch misleads maintainers into thinking the helper can return a failure result, and the duplicated error message invites divergent handling later.

[ADVISORY] The enablement predicate APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is hand-duplicated here and in refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5, and APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED in constants.ts is a truthy string rather than a boolean. A future gate added to one copy but not the other makes token parsing and token fetching disagree about the mode, silently applying the minimum schema to responses the refresh path did not source from the sync endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The redirect URI now hardcodes 'zoho-bigin' where it was derived from appConfig.slug, while callback.ts in the same app still reads the slug from config.json. The config slug and this literal are now two sources of truth for the same value; the next rename or config-driven slug change updates one and silently breaks the OAuth redirect.

[ADVISORY] The expiry computed on this rewritten path is Math.round(Date.now() + 60 * 60) — 3.6 seconds in milliseconds, not the 1 hour the comment implies (pre-existing arithmetic, but the diff rewrites the refresh that feeds it). Zoho CRM credentials are treated as expired immediately after every refresh, forcing a token refresh on every calendar operation.

[BUG] The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (ZodType has no toString override), so the schema is effectively `{access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown}` — the duplicate key overwrites the `z.number()` catch-all and the stated 'any property with a number is the expiry' behavior does not exist. In sharing mode every refresh response is parsed down to `{access_token}` alone because zod strips unknown keys — expiry_date/expires_in and refresh_token are silently dropped from every synced token, so persisted credentials never get a new expiry (perpetual refresh churn) and the placeholder refresh_token branch always fires; the sync feature's core data contract is not implemented.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{success, data, error}`), but this call site assigns the whole wrapper to `key` and persists it — the pre-diff code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`'s parsed data directly. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` in the database becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of the credential object; every subsequent read of `credential.key.access_token`/`.refresh_token` yields undefined, so Google Calendar API calls fail auth for that user until manual re-install — in both sharing and non-sharing modes.

[BUG] With credential sharing enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response of the sync endpoint, and `res?.data` on a fetch Response is undefined, so `token.access_token` on the next line throws a TypeError. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, any real expiry property from the refresh response will be dropped in sync mode, and the second computed key also overwrites the first, so even the intended `z.number()` constraint is lost. This makes the finding’s core claim (schema collapses and expiry isn’t kept / validation becomes too permissive) directly verifiable from the diff.

The use of `findFirst` (not `findUnique`) plus the inline comment “Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential” suggests there is no usable uniqueness key for an upsert here, making duplicates a realistic outcome and later `findFirst` results nondeterministic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The configured header name is used as-is to index req.headers, but Node lowercases all incoming header names, so an env value like 'Calcom-Webhook-Secret' looks up a key that never exists. adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the header is accessed as `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh under credential sharing crashes instead of refreshing, so synced google-calendar credentials fail all calendar operations once their initial expiry passes.
matched_golden_ids: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying bug: in the sync endpoint path, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response without a .data field, so res?.data is undefined and accessing token.access_token throws at runtime due to inconsistent return shape assumptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to fixed literal strings (Object.prototype.toString, i.e. '[object Object]'), not a catchall, so minimumTokenResponseSchema is a fixed-shape object that keeps only access_token and strips every other field — the expiry the adjacent comments promise is never captured. In sync mode every refreshed token is persisted without a fresh expiry (spread-based call sites like office365 and zoom retain the stale old expiryDate), so expiry-gated refresh fires on every calendar operation, hammering CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with one external call plus a credential write per request, or the expiry is undefined and 401s surface instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate at definition time to a single literal key (the ZodString object's `toString()` result, typically `"[object Object]"`), not a “catchall”. Zod `z.object()` also strips unknown keys by default, so this schema cannot capture arbitrary numeric expiry fields as the comments intend and will likely fail parsing unless the response literally contains that key. This directly breaks sync-mode token parsing (and can lead to missing/incorrect expiry handling in callers relying on the parsed data).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the parsed token has no refresh_token, the helper fabricates the literal string 'refresh_token' and the persisting call sites (google, office365calendar, zoomvideo spread it into the stored key) write it over the credential's real refresh token. In sync mode the stored refresh_token is destroyed on first refresh; any later fallback to local refresh — team credentials (userId null, which refreshOAuthTokens explicitly routes to the real refreshFunction) or an operator disabling credential sharing — authenticates with the literal 'refresh_token', the provider rejects it, and the credential is permanently broken until re-authentication.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same core bug: when refresh_token is missing, the parser/fetch logic sets it to the literal string "refresh_token", which then gets persisted/overwrites the real refresh token and causes subsequent refresh/authentication failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode the helper returns the raw fetch Response while each caller's fallback path returns a different type (google: GaxiosResponse .res, hubspot: HubspotToken, zoho: axios response), so no call site can consume both modes with one shape and the one-size sync contract cannot represent the per-provider token domains (expires_in vs expiry_date, refresh_token, instance_url). Every call site that does not natively consume a fetch Response breaks in sync mode — google crashes on token.access_token, hubspot wipes the credential key, zoho-bigin/zohocrm throw on .data.error, and the lark/msteams/webex parsers receive a body shape (access_token + expiry only) that lacks the provider fields they read.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` which, in sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), returns a native `fetch(...)` `Response` object, but in non-sync mode returns whatever the provider refresh function returns (e.g., Google uses `fetchTokens.res` with `.data`, Hubspot returns a `HubspotToken` object, Zoho returns an axios response with `.data`). Call sites are not updated to normalize this: e.g. GoogleCalendarService still does `const token = res?.data;` after `res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, which will be `undefined` for a `Response` and then `token.access_token` will crash. Hubspot assigns the return value to `HubspotToken`, but in sync mode it would be a `Response` (wrong shape). Zoho BigIn/CRM code expects `.data.error`, which a `Response` lacks. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` can fabricate `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing; in Office365 it merges this into existing credentials (`{...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data}`), potentially overwriting the real refresh token with the placeholder when sync mode returns only access_token/expiry, causing future refreshes to break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode the fetch Response returned by refreshOAuthTokens is bound to HubspotToken, so expiresIn/accessToken reads yield undefined and the persisted key collapses to {expiryDate: NaN} because a fetch Response has no own enumerable properties to spread. The first Hubspot token refresh under credential sharing wipes the stored credential key, destroying the access and refresh tokens and breaking the integration until the user re-authenticates.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a `Response`) without calling `.json()`. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. Under sync mode this value will be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, so any subsequent reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` / `expiresIn` (or spreading it into persisted credentials) will yield `undefined`/bad data and can corrupt the stored credential update. The diff shows this type/shape mismatch is introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The third argument passed to refreshOAuthTokens is credentialId (the credential row id) where the parameter is userId and every other call site in the diff passes credential.userId. The sync request carries calcomUserId=<credential id>, so the parent endpoint resolves the wrong (or no) user and can return another user's tokens into this credential row; team credentials also take the sync path because credentialId is always truthy, where every other app falls back to local refresh for them.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, while `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third parameter is explicitly `userId: number | null` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Every other modified call site in the diff passes `credential.userId`. If `credentialId` is the credential row id (as its name suggests), the sync request will send `calcomUserId=<credential id>` instead of the Cal.com user id, and it will also bypass the intended `userId`-null guard for non-user/team credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and the unchanged downstream check !tokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError. Zoho Bigin token refresh under credential sharing always fails, so synced credentials cannot refresh and calendar operations fail once the initial token expires.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`: `tokenInfo` is now assigned from `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(...)` (a `Response`), not an Axios response. Immediately after, the code still does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`, but `Response` has no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and accessing `.error` will throw a `TypeError`. Therefore Zoho Bigin token refresh will break under credential sharing/sync mode once it takes that branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and the unchanged check !zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error throws TypeError. Zoho CRM token refresh under credential sharing always fails, so synced credentials cannot refresh and calendar operations fail once the initial token expires.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, token refresh now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately dereferences `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` (e.g. `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`). But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. A `Response` object does not have a `.data` property, so in sync mode `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` will throw a `TypeError`. This is directly induced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips instance_url (and every field except access_token) from the Salesforce refresh response, and this update persists that stripped object as the credential key. After one refresh the stored key no longer contains instance_url, so the next connection creation reads credentialKey.instance_url as undefined and the jsforce connection cannot reach the Salesforce instance — Salesforce breaks from the second use onward under credential sharing.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, the function ignores the provided `schema` and instead `safeParse`s with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. Zod `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, so fields like Salesforce `instance_url` are dropped. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token is parsed via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` and then persisted with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }}})`. Under sync mode this stored `key` will no longer include `instance_url`, matching the finding’s claim that subsequent uses can break when code expects `credentialKey.instance_url` to exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A token refresh (external POST to login.salesforce.com plus a credential UPDATE) now runs unconditionally on every connection creation, where previously the jsforce.Connection was constructed locally and refreshed lazily by jsforce on 401. Every availability check or booking flow that instantiates the service now pays a Salesforce token-endpoint round trip and a DB write even when the token is valid, and concurrent service instances race duplicate refreshes and writes on the same credential row.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then unconditionally performs `prisma.credential.update(...)` before constructing and returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no check for token validity/expiry nor any conditional path to skip refresh, so every instantiation of the service will incur an external round trip and a DB write even when the existing access token is still valid. This also introduces an obvious risk of concurrent instances triggering duplicate refreshes and updates against the same credential row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler trusts the parent's raw numeric userId to identify the local user (the schema comment says 'UserId of the cal.com user') with no cross-instance identity mapping or verification such as an email check. Unless the child instance's user id space is kept identical to cal.com's, the webhook delivers one cal.com user's OAuth credentials to the local user holding the same numeric id — a different person — who then books meetings through another user's calendar; any user created or deleted on either side diverges the id spaces and nothing in the design detects it.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the request schema requires a raw numeric `userId` and the handler directly looks up and writes credentials by that local `id` (`prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } })` and then `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, ... } })`). There is no cross-instance identity verification (e.g., email/UUID mapping) or any check that the `userId` refers to the same person across systems. If the sending system’s user ID space differs from the receiving instance’s, credentials could be created/updated for the wrong local user who happens to share that numeric ID, which is a real security/correctness risk grounded in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The findFirst-then-create sequence is a check-then-insert race with no UNIQUE(userId, appId) constraint backing it (the in-code claim that upsert is impossible is exactly the missing unique key), and the (userId, appId) slot also has a second writer in the local OAuth callback. Two concurrent webhook deliveries (e.g., a reconnect racing an in-flight sync) both miss the findFirst and create duplicate Credential rows for the same user and app, and the findFirst can also overwrite the key of a locally-installed credential; consumers binding to a stale duplicate use dead tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, credentials are written using a non-atomic `findFirst` then `create` sequence keyed by `{ userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }`. This is inherently racy: two concurrent requests can both observe no row and both execute `prisma.credential.create(...)`, producing duplicate credential rows unless the DB enforces a UNIQUE constraint on `(userId, appId)` (no such constraint is shown in this diff), and there is no retry/unique-violation handling. Even if a unique constraint exists, this code would still intermittently 500 on concurrent deliveries. The comment “Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id” further suggests the code is not relying on a unique key, increasing the likelihood of duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws ZodError unhandled, and there is no method guard so req.body is undefined on GET, returning a 500 for malformed requests while the handler's own 403/404 paths establish a 4xx contract. Any malformed POST — or any GET — to /api/webhook/app-credential returns a 500 instead of a 400, masking client errors as server faults.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is called without any `try/catch` or centralized error wrapper. In Next.js API routes, a thrown `ZodError` will result in a 500 response. There is also no `req.method` guard, so a `GET` request (where `req.body` is typically `undefined`/empty) will hit the `parse` call and throw, returning 500 instead of a 4xx. This contradicts the handler’s explicit 403/404 4xx response contract for client errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The credential-sync endpoint becomes a hard, unguarded dependency of the token-refresh path: the fetch has no timeout, no response.ok check, and the design provides no fallback once the placeholder refresh token has replaced the real one. If the parent cal.com instance is slow or down, every calendar operation needing a refresh hangs (Node fetch has no default timeout) or fails with an HTML error page flowing into the token parsers — a cascading failure across all shared-credential apps with no degradation path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new token-refresh branch via `refreshOAuthTokens()` that, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, performs a bare `fetch()` to the sync endpoint and returns the raw `Response` without any `response.ok` check or JSON parsing, and with no timeout (Node fetch has none by default): `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`. Several call sites expect non-`Response` shapes (e.g., HubSpot expects a `HubspotToken` object; Zoho expects an Axios response with `.data`; Google expects `res.data`), so the shared-credential path can break at runtime. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` forcibly injects a dummy refresh token when missing (`refresh_token = "refresh_token"`), and Office365 then merges and persists that into the credential record (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), which can overwrite the real refresh token and cause subsequent refreshes to fail with no fallback. These are concrete, diff-grounded correctness/availability defects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The child-to-parent sync request carries no authentication material — no secret header or signature, only calcomUserId and appSlug in the body — so the integration contract as defined can only be served by an endpoint that authenticates callers out of band or not at all. Self-hosters following the .env.example stand up a credential-delivery endpoint whose contract gives it nothing to authenticate the caller with; access control is left entirely to deployment-specific mechanisms the shipped client never exercises.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the outgoing sync call in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` posts only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no authentication headers/signature. The newly added `.env.example` values (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`) are used for the *incoming* webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), not for this outgoing sync request. So the finding is grounded: the provided client-side contract for the credential-sync endpoint does not include any built-in auth material, pushing access control to deployment-specific mechanisms. This is a meaningful security/architecture concern, though not a guaranteed functional defect in Cal.com itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Salesforce is the only refreshed app not routed through refreshOAuthTokens — it refreshes directly against login.salesforce.com even when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured. A parallel refresh path contradicts the feature's own architecture: self-hosters configuring sync still get direct Salesforce calls from the child using parent-shared refresh tokens, and credential rotation performed on the parent never propagates to salesforce credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh path is a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` with no use of the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper or any conditional on `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`/`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`. Other integrations in this diff were explicitly routed through `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` to support the sync endpoint. So when sync is configured, Salesforce will still refresh against Salesforce directly, contradicting the newly introduced sync architecture.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new sync-mode branching logic (mode-dependent schema selection, placeholder injection, wrapper return shape) ships with no test anywhere in the diff, and the google call site already mis-binds its return value. Regressions in this helper corrupt persisted credentials across every calendar and video app at once; a single test asserting the returned shape and the persisted key would have caught the google wrapper bug before ship.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new helper is misused: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` assigns the *Zod safeParse result object* (`{ success, data|error }`) to `key`, and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Other call sites (e.g. Office365) treat `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` as a safeParse return and extract `.data`, but Google does not—so this diff introduces a real, verifiable corruption of persisted Google credential `key` shape. The finding’s note about missing tests is secondary but consistent with this concrete bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The decrypted keys payload is persisted without validating it against the target app's credential schema (each app ships one, e.g. googleCredentialSchema), and a decryption or JSON.parse failure surfaces as an unhandled 500. Parent/child version skew or a buggy parent silently persists malformed credentials that only fail at booking time, far from the write that caused them; a schema parse at this boundary would reject bad payloads with a 400.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted `keys` are produced via `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` with no try/catch. If decryption fails (e.g., wrong key, malformed ciphertext) or JSON.parse fails, the handler will throw and Next.js will return an unhandled 500. Also, the resulting `keys` object is written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `key: keys` without validating against any app-specific credential schema (only `appStoreMetadata` is consulted, which provides `slug`/`type` but no schema validation). This matches the finding that malformed payloads could be persisted and only fail later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The !accessTokenParsed.success branch is dead code — parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on parse failure, so the Promise.reject is unreachable. The unreachable branch misleads maintainers into thinking the helper can return a failure result, and the duplicated error message invites divergent handling later.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` calls `safeParse(...)` and immediately `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `!refreshTokenResponse.success`. Therefore it can only return a successful Zod result. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the subsequent check `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) { return Promise.reject(...) }` is unreachable dead code, which can mislead maintainers about the helper’s behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The enablement predicate APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is hand-duplicated here and in refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5, and APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED in constants.ts is a truthy string rather than a boolean. A future gate added to one copy but not the other makes token parsing and token fetching disagree about the mode, silently applying the minimum schema to responses the refresh path did not source from the sync endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate, slightly different gates for “sync mode”: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, while `refreshOAuthTokens` additionally requires `userId` (`... && userId`). That means parsing can enter the “minimum schema” path even when the refresh did not use the sync endpoint (e.g., when `userId` is null), so the finding about duplicated predicates diverging is grounded. Also `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which yields a truthy string/undefined rather than an explicit boolean. However, the claim about a future gate being added is speculative, and the diff alone doesn’t prove a current user-visible failure—so this is best classified as a concrete maintainability/correctness risk rather than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The redirect URI now hardcodes 'zoho-bigin' where it was derived from appConfig.slug, while callback.ts in the same app still reads the slug from config.json. The config slug and this literal are now two sources of truth for the same value; the next rename or config-driven slug change updates one and silently breaks the OAuth redirect.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts` the redirect URI was changed from using `appConfig.slug` to a hardcoded `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback`, while `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/callback.ts` still imports `appConfig` from `config.json` (implying the slug remains config-driven elsewhere). The diff doesn’t prove a current mismatch, but it does create two potential sources of truth for the slug, increasing the risk of a future rename/config change silently breaking the OAuth redirect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The expiry computed on this rewritten path is Math.round(Date.now() + 60 * 60) — 3.6 seconds in milliseconds, not the 1 hour the comment implies (pre-existing arithmetic, but the diff rewrites the refresh that feeds it). Zoho CRM credentials are treated as expired immediately after every refresh, forcing a token refresh on every calendar operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code sets `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + 60 * 60);` while the surrounding comment says it’s setting an expiry offset (implying ~1 hour). Since `Date.now()` is milliseconds, adding `60*60` only adds 3600ms (3.6s), which would make the stored expiry nearly immediate if later compared against `Date.now()`-style timestamps. This line is present in the diff context of the rewritten refresh flow, so the PR still contains this likely-expiry bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (ZodType has no toString override), so the schema is effectively `{access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown}` — the duplicate key overwrites the `z.number()` catch-all and the stated 'any property with a number is the expiry' behavior does not exist. In sharing mode every refresh response is parsed down to `{access_token}` alone because zod strips unknown keys — expiry_date/expires_in and refresh_token are silently dropped from every synced token, so persisted credentials never get a new expiry (perpetual refresh churn) and the placeholder refresh_token branch always fires; the sync feature's core data contract is not implemented.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the object schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Since `z.string()` returns an object and Zod types don’t override `toString()`, both keys evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"`, and the second one overwrites the first. The resulting schema is effectively `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`, so it does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” behavior, nor does it preserve `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`refresh_token` in sharing mode (Zod will strip unknown keys by default). This makes the parsing/contract incorrect in the added sharing-mode token refresh path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{success, data, error}`), but this call site assigns the whole wrapper to `key` and persists it — the pre-diff code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`'s parsed data directly. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` in the database becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}` instead of the credential object; every subsequent read of `credential.key.access_token`/`.refresh_token` yields undefined, so Google Calendar API calls fail auth for that user until manual re-install — in both sharing and non-sharing modes.

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, error }`) rather than the parsed credential data. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff changes `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials);` to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That will store the wrapper object into `credential.key`, changing its shape and breaking later code that expects `credential.key.access_token` etc. This is verifiable directly from the new helper implementation and its call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With credential sharing enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response of the sync endpoint, and `res?.data` on a fetch Response is undefined, so `token.access_token` on the next line throws a TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh on a sharing-enabled deployment throws inside the try block and never persists new tokens, so calendar operations fall back to the expired access token and start returning 401s — the flagship integration of this sync feature is broken in its own happy path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In Google Calendar refresh (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), the code then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`, but a `fetch` Response has no `.data` field (and the body is never `await res.json()`). This makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime on sharing-enabled deployments, preventing token persistence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With sharing enabled the awaited value of refreshOAuthTokens is a fetch Response, not the HubspotToken the variable annotation and the following expiry math assume, so `expires_in`, `access_token` and `refresh_token` property reads all yield undefined. HubSpot token refresh under sharing persists `expiryDate: NaN` and a credential key containing no access token, leaving the credential permanently expired and every HubSpot calendar operation failing once the initial token expires.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it does `await fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The helper returns two incompatible shapes — a raw fetch Response in sharing mode versus the provider-specific object (googleauth res, HubspotToken, axios response) otherwise — with an untyped `refreshFunction: () => any` and no defined schema for the sync endpoint's response body. adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns different, incompatible types depending on the branch: in sharing mode it returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, lines returning `response` from `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`), but otherwise it returns whatever the integration-specific `refreshFunction()` returns (gaxios/Google `res`, HubSpot `HubspotToken`, axios response, etc.). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The literal string "refresh_token" is persisted as the credential's refresh_token whenever the parsed response lacks one, overwriting whatever refresh token was previously stored. The real refresh token is destroyed in the database on the first shared refresh, so toggling credential sharing off later — or running with sharing on but CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT unset, which silently falls back to the local refreshFunction — leaves every synced credential permanently unable to refresh without per-user re-authentication; the env toggle is a one-way door.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when the parsed token response lacks `refresh_token`, the code forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gates the webhook write path on CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY but not on CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, while the refresh path in refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse additionally requires the endpoint. An operator who sets the two webhook vars but leaves the endpoint empty (the .env.example ships all four with empty defaults) gets a deployment that accepts credential writes but refreshes locally against placeholder or stale tokens — a partially-enabled state that only fails at first token expiry, far from the config that caused it.

adjudication.rationale: Diff-grounded mismatch: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined only by `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), and the webhook write handler is gated solely on that (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts). This creates a partially-enabled configuration state (webhook accepts/updates credentials while refresh logic won’t use the external endpoint). Whether it becomes a runtime failure depends on what keys are synced (webhook doesn’t validate key shape), so it’s more of an operational/edge-case footgun than a strictly provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse run with no try/catch and the decrypted value is persisted without validation against the app's credential schema, so a wrong-key or malformed payload throws into a 500 while any decryptable JSON value is written as the credential key and acknowledged with 200. A parent/child encryption key mismatch turns every sync delivery into an unhandled 500, and a malformed-but-decryptable payload silently replaces a working credential with garbage while returning 200, so the sender believes sync succeeded and the user's integration is bricked without any error signal.

Also, any decryptable JSON value is written directly to `credential.key` via `prisma.credential.update/create` without validating shape against any app credential schema (only the outer webhook body is zod-validated), so a malformed-but-JSON payload can overwrite a previously working credential while the endpoint still returns 200.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The prisma.app.findUnique queries only to select the slug that was just read from the request body, which is then used to index appStoreMetadata — `appStoreMetadata[reqBody.appSlug]` alone is equivalent. Every webhook delivery pays a pointless DB round-trip and carries a dead branch plus an `as keyof typeof` cast; deleting the query, the `if (!app)` check and the cast removes ten lines with no behavior change since the App table is seeded from the same metadata source.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), it does `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug }, select: { slug: true } })` and then immediately uses only that `slug` to index `appStoreMetadata` (`appStoreMetadata[app.slug as ...]`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The findFirst-without-orderBy followed by a non-atomic find-then-create means two concurrent deliveries for the same userId+appSlug both observe no credential and both take the create branch. A bulk initial sync of many users produces duplicate Credential rows for the same user and app; which duplicate downstream credential resolution picks is DB-order-dependent, causing flaky credential selection that is hard to diagnose.

With concurrent webhook deliveries for the same `(userId, appSlug)`, both requests can observe “no row” and both execute the create branch, producing duplicate credential rows if the DB does not enforce a unique constraint. The code comment (“Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id”) further indicates there is no atomic uniqueness-based upsert being used here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook secret is compared with a plain `!==` string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison, and the endpoint has no rate limiting. The early-exit comparison leaks timing signal on the shared secret to a client iterating the header value on a network-exposed endpoint; a staff-level hardening pass would use timingSafeEqual on hashed values before this ships as a credential-write primitive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens POSTs calcomUserId and appSlug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication header, signature, or shared secret, so the sync endpoint can only hand out a user's OAuth access tokens to unauthenticated callers. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, googlecalendar's `const token = res?.data` yields undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError, zoho-bigin/zohocrm's `tokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError on the Response object, and hubspot reads undefined fields off the Response (NaN expiry, undefined tokens persisted) — token refresh for those integrations fails or corrupts stored credentials on every attempt.

The callers in this diff continue to treat the returned value as provider-shaped: e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data;` (expects axios/googleapis-style `.data`) but in sharing mode `res` is a `Response` with no `.data`, so `token` becomes undefined and `token.access_token` will throw. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]', so minimumTokenResponseSchema is a plain object schema whose only real field is access_token, and Zod's default strip mode drops every other property of the token response. When credential sharing is enabled, parseRefreshTokenResponse validates nothing but access_token and silently strips the fields callers persist: Salesforce's stored credential loses instance_url/id/scope (breaking the jsforce connection after the credential is reloaded), and for credentials with a null userId (team credentials) the real provider response is loose-parsed, overwriting the stored refresh_token with the literal placeholder 'refresh_token' and permanently destroying the user's refresh token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, but `z.string()` is a Zod object whose `.toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"`. This means the schema does not actually allow arbitrary expiry fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `expires_in`) and, because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default, `safeParse` will drop all provider fields other than `access_token` (and the unusable `"[object Object]"` key). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook secret is compared with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison, exposing a timing side channel on the secret that guards arbitrary-user credential writes. A remote attacker with network access to the endpoint can statistically distinguish prefix-matching secret candidates byte by byte; since a correct guess grants the ability to overwrite every user's app credentials, the comparison should use crypto.timingSafeEqual as standard webhook verifiers do.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check uses a direct equality comparison: `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and returns 403 on mismatch. This is a plain string/byte comparison (not constant-time) guarding a high-impact operation (creating/updating arbitrary users’ credentials via `prisma.credential.update/create`). The diff shows no use of `crypto.timingSafeEqual` or similar constant-time verification, so the timing side-channel concern is directly applicable to this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, whose runtime value is the credential-encryption key string itself rather than a boolean. Any future code that logs, serializes, or passes this 'flag' into client-facing props (constants.ts is imported by client components) leaks the AES credential-encryption key, and its truthy-string semantics mean values like 'false' enable the feature instead of disabling it.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/lib/constants.ts the new export `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED = process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;` will evaluate to the *encryption key string* (second operand) when both env vars are set, not a boolean. The diff shows this value is used as a flag (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` in the new webhook handler and in `parseRefreshTokenResponse` / `refreshOAuthTokens`), so the type/semantics are a footgun and could lead to accidental leakage if later logged/serialized. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The documented key-generation command `openssl rand -base64 24` produces 24 bytes of key material (a 32-character base64 string), contradicting the adjacent 'must be 32 bytes for AES256' requirement. symmetricDecrypt base64-decodes the key string before createDecipheriv('aes-256-cbc', ...) (the same convention that makes the documented `openssl rand -base64 32` CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY work), so a self-hoster following this documented command supplies a 24-byte key, every decryption throws 'Invalid key length', and every credential-sync webhook call returns 500 — the feature is dead on arrival for anyone who sets the key per the instructions.
