The new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) unconditionally calls `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` with no length/format validation, so a self-hoster following the provided instructions is very likely to configure an invalid-length key for AES-256 and trigger runtime decryption failures, breaking the credential sync flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler's zod .parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse calls all run without try/catch, so malformed request bodies, undecryptable ciphertexts, and non-JSON decrypted plaintexts escape as unhandled exceptions. Invalid input that should yield a 4xx returns a 500 instead (triggering webhook retries), and a mismatched CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY between the two instances turns every sync call into an indistinguishable 500 rather than an actionable configuration error.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` will throw on malformed input, and both `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)` and the subsequent `JSON.parse(...)` can throw on undecryptable ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext. There is no surrounding try/catch or error-to-4xx mapping, so these cases will bubble up as unhandled exceptions and return a 500. This matches the finding that invalid input or a mismatched `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` would result in indistinguishable 500s rather than actionable 4xx responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint concentrates write access to every local user's app credentials behind a single reusable bearer header value with no HMAC binding over the body, no replay protection, no rate limiting, and no audit trail, and it persists the decrypted payload without any schema validation. Leakage of the one secret (via logs, proxies, or the parent instance) lets an attacker silently rewrite any user's credentials — including redirecting Stripe payments or calendar events to attacker-controlled accounts — and replay captured requests indefinitely; unlike standard webhook verifiers, nothing binds the secret to the request body, and the decrypted JSON is stored as credential.key without the schema validation the OAuth callback path applies.

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authorizes writes solely by comparing a static shared secret in a configurable header (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] === CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), with no signature/HMAC over the body, no nonce/timestamp/replay protection, and no evident rate limiting or auditing in this handler. It then decrypts `reqBody.keys` and `JSON.parse`s it and directly persists it as `credential.key` via Prisma (`data: { key: keys }`) without any schema validation of the decrypted payload. The request body includes an arbitrary `userId`, so anyone with the one secret can update/create credentials for any local user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Salesforce token refresh now runs unconditionally inside the connection-building path on every CalendarService construction, adding a network round-trip to login.salesforce.com plus a credential-table write per service instantiation even when credential sharing is disabled. Every calendar read/write for Salesforce users pays an extra provider round-trip and DB write on each service construction (previously jsforce refreshed lazily on demand), multiplying provider rate-limit pressure and credential-row churn under booking load.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token HTTP call to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` plus a `prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no guard on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, and the refresh/update occur on this code path every time the service constructs/initializes its connection, which can add an extra provider round-trip and DB write per instantiation (a performance/rate-limit/DB-churn concern rather than a direct correctness defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler resolves reqBody.userId — the calling instance's user id — directly against the local user table with no cross-instance identity mapping or scoping beyond the shared secret. In sharing mode every parsed refresh response reduces to {access_token} plus the injected refresh_token literal: office365-calendar persists refresh_token: "refresh_token" over the real refresh token (spread at office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264), salesforce loses instance_url, and expiry fields (expires_in/expiry_date) never reach the stored credential.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the object keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are evaluated at JS runtime as a single literal property name (effectively `"[object Object]"`), and the second one overwrites the first in the object literal. So `minimumTokenResponseSchema` does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” behavior; in Zod’s default `strip` mode it will accept only `access_token` (and possibly a `"[object Object]"` field) while stripping real fields like `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc. Because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` also injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing, callers like `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` spread `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials, overwriting the real refresh token with the literal string when sharing mode is enabled. Similarly, `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` will drop non-access-token fields from the refreshed token response in sharing mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With sharing enabled accessTokenParsed.data contains only {access_token, refresh_token: 'refresh_token'} (the minimum schema strips the rest), so the persisted key loses instance_url, id, issued_at, signature, scope and token_type. The next jsforce.Connection is built with instanceUrl undefined, so subsequent Salesforce API calls target the wrong base URL and the integration fails after the first refresh under sharing mode.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it validates using `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not include fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature`, `scope`, `token_type`) and Zod `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token is persisted via `data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }`, so under sharing mode the stored credential key would lose those extra Salesforce fields. On subsequent runs, `credential.key` would no longer contain `instance_url`, making `jsforce.Connection` construction prone to `instanceUrl` being undefined and breaking API calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no AbortSignal timeout, so a hung parent sync endpoint stalls the token-refresh path with no bound. Calendar availability and booking operations that need a token refresh block for up to the platform's default idle timeouts (minutes) per call whenever the parent cal.com endpoint is slow or down, turning a remote outage into local request stalls on the booking path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` without any timeout/`AbortSignal` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple calendar/video services now await this call during token refresh (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Webex/etc.), so a slow/hung sync endpoint can stall request handling. This is a concrete resilience/performance concern grounded in the diff, though not a strictly incorrect behavior in terms of functional correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The findFirst-then-create sequence is not atomic, so two concurrent or retried webhook deliveries for the same userId+appSlug can both observe no existing credential and both take the create branch. Duplicate Credential rows accumulate for the same user and app (or the duplicate insert is rejected as a 500 if a unique index exists); subsequent syncs update whichever row findFirst returns first, leaving duplicates stale and credential resolution nondeterministic.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the code checks for an existing credential via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug }})` and then conditionally calls `prisma.credential.create(...)` if none is found. This check-then-act sequence is not atomic and is vulnerable to concurrent/retried webhook deliveries: two requests can both see no row and both attempt `create`, producing duplicate credential rows (if no unique constraint) or triggering an insertion failure (if a unique constraint exists). The finding accurately describes nondeterministic updates because subsequent syncs use `findFirst` and will update an arbitrary matching row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new token fetch runs unconditionally on every connection creation — no expiry check, no APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED gate, and no timeout — replacing jsforce's lazy refresh-on-401 with a per-operation round trip plus credential write. Every Salesforce calendar operation now costs an extra outbound token request and a DB write even when the stored token is still valid, adding latency and avoidable rate-limit exposure on login.salesforce.com, and a refresh-endpoint hiccup now fails operations that previously would have succeeded on the still-valid stored token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` *before* returning the `jsforce.Connection` (lines added around the `fetch(...)`, `await response.json()`, and DB update). There is no expiry/validity check on the stored token prior to refreshing, no use of the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper / `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` gating in this path, and the `fetch` has no explicit timeout/abort handling. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/reliability concern (extra outbound call + DB write and new failure point) even if it may be an intentional design change rather than a strict correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Success is detected with response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok/response.status, so any 200 whose reason phrase is not exactly 'OK' (HTTP/2 upstreams report an empty statusText; intermediaries can rewrite it) is misclassified as a failure. A successful Salesforce token response would throw HttpError 400 and fail the calendar operation despite the refresh having succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the newly added refresh flow checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. This is incorrect because `statusText` is not a reliable indicator of HTTP success (it can be empty or different even when `response.ok` is true). As a result, a successful token refresh (e.g., HTTP 200 with non-"OK"/empty reason phrase) would be misclassified as failure and throw `HttpError 400`, breaking Salesforce calendar operations despite a successful refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The helper throws on parse failure yet returns the SafeParseReturnType, so success is always true at every call site — salesforce's `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` is unreachable dead code and office365's `tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data` guard is always-true. Readers of these call sites assume failure is signalled through the result object and can add handling that never runs; the dead branch in salesforce advertises error handling that does not exist.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the helper calls `schema.safeParse(...)` but immediately `throw`s when `!refreshTokenResponse.success`, so any return value necessarily has `success: true`. Yet call sites treat the return as a normal `SafeParseReturnType`: e.g. Salesforce does `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) { ... }` after calling `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, which is unreachable, and Office365 uses `(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` which is redundant because failure would have thrown earlier. This is diff-grounded misleading/dead-branch logic, though it doesn’t by itself prove a runtime defect in the new behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The helper's return value is a union of a raw fetch Response (sharing branch) and whatever the provider-specific refreshFunction returns, with refreshFunction typed `() => any`, so TypeScript cannot flag call sites that consume the two branches differently. Four call sites (google, hubspot, zoho-bigin, zohocrm) compiled while reading token fields or .data off a fetch Response; the next app converted to this helper will repeat the same mistake unless the two branches are split into separately-typed functions.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` in the sharing branch, but returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns in the normal branch (typed `() => any`). Several updated call sites assume the returned value has provider-specific shapes like `.data` (Axios/Gaxios) or token fields: e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, Zoho Bigin checks `tokenInfo.data.error`, and Zoho CRM checks `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. If `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, these will receive a `Response` object (no `.data`), causing broken behavior at runtime, and TypeScript won’t catch it due to `any`/union behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The removed console.error block means a failed token parse now surfaces only the context-free 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with neither the zod issue nor the Microsoft response logged. When the new minimum-schema or provider-schema parse rejects a real Microsoft response, on-call debugging has no record of what the provider returned, misdirecting investigation of Outlook token failures introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the prior `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens...", tokenResponse.error, "MS response:", responseJson)` block was removed when switching from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. The new helper (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) throws a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure and does not log the Zod error details or the provider response. This is a diff-grounded observability/debuggability regression rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The outbound sync request carries no authentication material at all (no secret header, unlike the sibling webhook endpoint in this diff which gates on CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET), so the parent's sync endpoint must be fully unauthenticated for this to work. If the parent endpoint applies the same secret check as the webhook in this diff, every sharing-mode token refresh fails with 403 and all synced integrations break; if it does not, the endpoint hands out any user's credentials to any caller — either way the contract gap bites.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sharing-mode is enabled it POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only a form body (`calcomUserId`, `appSlug`) and no authentication headers or secret material. This contrasts with the new inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) which explicitly gates on a secret header (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). As written, a parent sync endpoint that enforces the same secret check would 403 and break token refresh, while an endpoint that doesn't enforce auth would be effectively unauthenticated from Cal.com's side. The lack of any auth material in the outbound request is directly verifiable in the diff.
